verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary: 34:1 This is literally a marker for a new revelation.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要向以色列的牧人发预言，攻击他们，说，主耶和华如此说：祸哉！以色列的牧人只知牧养自己。牧人岂不当牧养群羊吗？
verses.en: “Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds[NOTE:1] of Israel; prophesy, and say to them—to the shepherds: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been feeding themselves! Should not shepherds feed the flock?
notes: The term shepherd is applied to kings in the ancient Near East. In the OT the Lord is often addressed as shepherd of Israel (Gen 49:24; Ps 8:1). The imagery of shepherds as Israel’s leaders is also employed (Jer 23:1-2).
verses.commentary:
34:2 "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

Special Topic: Son of Man

▣ "prophesy" This term (BDB 612, KB 659) is first used in Ezek. 4:7 (Niphal PERFECT, cf. Ezek. 37:7),
but it appears often as a Niphal IMPERATIVE (cf. Ezek. 6:2; 11:4[twice]; 13:2,17; 20:46; 21:2,9,14,28; 25:2; 28:21; 29:2;
30:2; 34:2[twice]; 35:2; 36:1,3,6; 37:9[twice],12; 38:2,14; 39:1).

Special Topic: Prophecy (OT)

▣ "the shepherds of Israel" "Shepherd" (BDB 944, KB 1258, Qal PARTICIPLE, cf. Ezek. 34:2 [6 times],
3, 5,7,8 [3 times],9,10,12,23 [twice]) refers to the leaders, both political (i.e. 2 Sam. 7:7) and religious (i.e. priests, cf. Isa. 56:11; prophets, cf. Jer. 23:1-4;
both Jer. 23:9-10; Zech. 11:17; and king, cf. Ezekiel 22).

This VERB also occurs in

- Qal IMPERFECT, Ezek. 34:2, 3, 8,10,14 (twice),15,16,18,19,23 (twice)

- Qal PERFECT, Ezek. 34:8,12,13,23

- Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, Ezek. 34:10

The origin of this concept comes

- from the pastoral traditions of the Patriarchs (cf. Genesis 49:24)

- Moses was a shepherd (cf. Exod. 3:1)

- from David's early life as a family herdsman (i.e. 1 Samuel 16:11; Psalm 78:70-71)

- Ultimately YHWH is the "good shepherd" (cf. Ps. 23; 77:20; 78:52; 80:1; Isa. 40:11; Jer. 23:3; 31:10.

- The Davidic Messiah ‒ Jer. 23:5-6; Ezek. 34:20-24; Matt. 2:6; John 10:11,14-16; Heb. 13:20; 1 Pet. 2:5; 5:4; Rev. 7:17

Sheep are animals that need constant care and protection. Shepherding became a powerful image for this (i.e. Gen. 49:24 Psalm 23).

Zechariah also uses the concept of true and evil shepherds in an eschatological, apocalyptic setting (cf. Zechariah 11-13).

Special Topic: Titles for the Special Coming One

Special Topic: Apocalyptic Literature

verses.zh: 你们吃脂油、穿羊毛、宰肥壮的，却不牧养群羊。
verses.en: You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the choice animals, but you do not feed the sheep!
verses.commentary:
34:3-4 These false shepherds think more of their own well-being than they do of the people of YHWH (cf. Jer. 23:1-6; 50:6).

- feed (lit. pasturing) themselves, Ezek. 34:2,8,10

- eat the fat of the sheep, Ezek. 34:3,10 (possibly referring to milk products)

- take the wool, Ezek. 34:3

- do not feed the flock, Ezek. 34:3

- do not help the sick, Ezek. 34:4

- do not bind the broken, Ezek. 34:4

- do not seek the scattered, Ezek. 34:4

- treat the flock violently, Ezek. 34:4

34:3 "the fat" These CONSONANTS (חלב) can be revocalized as "milk" (LXX, Vulgate), referring to butter,
cheese, or cream. The UBS Text Project, p. 117, gives "milk" a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

verses.zh: 瘦弱的，你们没有养壮；有病的，你们没有医治；受伤的，你们没有缠裹；被逐的，你们没有领回；失丧的，你们没有寻找；但用强暴严严地辖制。
verses.en: You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bandaged the injured, brought back the strays, or sought the lost, but with force and harshness[NOTE:1] you have ruled over them.
notes: The term translated “harshness” is used to describe the oppression the Israelites suffered as slaves in Egypt (Exod 1:13).
verses.commentary:
34:4 "but with force and with severity you have dominated them" Note the three terms which denote the cruel treatment.

- with force, BDB 306, cf. Jdg. 4:3; 8:1; 2 Sam. 2:16

- with severity, BDB 827, cf. Exod. 1:13,14; Lev. 25:43,46,53

- dominated, BDB 921, KB 1109, Qal PERFECT, cf.
Lev. 25:53; 26:17 (this is the same root used in Gen. 1:26,28)

verses.zh: 因无牧人，羊就分散；既分散，便作了一切野兽的食物。
verses.en: They were scattered because they had no shepherd, and they became food for every wild beast.[NOTE:1]
notes: As a case of dittography, the MT repeats “and they were scattered” at the end of the verse.
verses.commentary:
34:5-6 As a result of the action, or lack of action, of leaders, the people of YHWH

- are scattered (cf. Jer. 23:1-2)

- are preyed on (cf. Ezek. 34:8,23; 14:15,21)

- wandered away and no one searched for them

Sheep usually stay together. For them to be scattered demonstrates a stressful, dangerous situation.

34:5 "they are scattered for lack of a shepherd" Also refer to Num. 27:17; 1 Kgs. 22:17; and Matt. 9:36.

verses.zh: 我的羊在诸山间、在各高冈上流离，在全地上分散，无人去寻，无人去找。
verses.en: My sheep wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My sheep were scattered over the entire face of the earth with no one looking or searching for them.
verses.commentary:
34:6 "there was no one to search or seek for them" The term "search" (BDB 205,
KB 233, Qal PARTICIPLE) is used several times in this chapter.

- Judah's leaders did not seek, Ezek. 34:6

- the shepherds did not seek (BDB 205, KB 233, Qal PERFECT), Ezek. 34:8

- YHWH will require (BDB 205, KB 233, Qal PERFECT with waw) His sheep, Ezek. 34:10

- YHWH, Himself will search (BDB 205, KB 233, Qal PERFECT with waw) for His sheep, Ezek. 34:11

The word "search" is parallel in this verse with "seek" (BDB 134, KB 152, Piel PARTICIPLE,
cf. Jdg. 6:29; 1 Chr. 16:11; 2 Chr. 20:3-4; Job 10:6; Ps. 24:6; 38:12; 105:4; Jer. 29:13)

Special Topic: Seek the Lord

verses.zh: 「所以，你们这些牧人要听耶和华的话。
verses.en: “‘Therefore, you shepherds, listen to the Lord’s message:
verses.commentary: 34:7-10 This surely is an example of individual responsibility and divine judgment. This individual aspect is characteristic of Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 18).

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我的羊因无牧人就成为掠物，也作了一切野兽的食物。我的牧人不寻找我的羊；这些牧人只知牧养自己，并不牧养我的羊。
verses.en: As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, my sheep have become prey and have become food for all the wild beasts. There was no shepherd, and my shepherds did not search for my flock, but fed themselves and did not feed my sheep.

verses.zh: 所以你们这些牧人要听耶和华的话。
verses.en: Therefore, you shepherds, listen to the Lord’s message.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我必与牧人为敌，必向他们的手追讨我的羊，使他们不再牧放群羊；牧人也不再牧养自己。我必救我的羊脱离他们的口，不再作他们的食物。」
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look, I am against the shepherds, and I will demand my sheep from their hand. I will no longer let them be shepherds;[NOTE:1] the shepherds will not feed themselves anymore. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, so that they will no longer be food for them.
notes: Heb “I will cause them to cease from feeding sheep.”

verses.zh: 「主耶和华如此说：看哪，我必亲自寻找我的羊，将它们寻见。
verses.en: “‘For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look, I myself will search for my sheep and seek them out.
verses.commentary:
34:11-31 Notice the number of FIRST PERSON MASCULINE SINGULAR statements!
YHWH, Himself will act on behalf of His people. This is exactly the opposite of Ezek. 34:2-6.

- I Myself will search for My sheep, Ezek. 34:11

- I Myself will seek them out, Ezek. 34:11

- I will care for My sheep, Ezek. 34:12

- I will deliver them, Ezek. 34:12,22

- I will bring them out from the peoples, Ezek. 34:13 (cf. Ezek. 11:17; 20:41)

- I will gather them, Ezek. 34:13 (cf. Ezek. 11:17; 20:34.41; 28:25; 36:24; 37:21; 38:8; 39:27)

- I will feed them, Ezek. 34:13,14,15,18

- I will lead them to rest (lit. "cause to lie down"), Ezek. 34:15 (cf. Ps. 23:1,2)

- I will seek the lost, Ezek. 34:16

- I will bring back the scattered, Ezek. 34:16

- I will bind up the broken, Ezek. 34:16 (cf. Isa. 30:26)

- I will strengthen the sick, Ezek. 34:16 (cf. Ps. 147:3)

- I will feed them judgment, Ezek. 34:16

- I will judge between one sheep and another, Ezek. 34:17,22

- I will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep, Ezek. 34:20 (cf. Ezek. 34:16)

- I will set over them one shepherd, My servant David

- I will be their God, Ezek. 34:24

- I will make a covenant of peace with them, Ezek. 34:25

- I will eliminate harmful beasts, Ezek. 34:25

- I will make them and the places around My hill a blessing, Ezek. 34:26

- I will cause showers to come down in their season, Ezek. 34:26

- I have broken the bars of their yoke, Ezek. 34:27

- I have delivered them, Ezek. 34:27

- I will establish for them a renowned planting place, Ezek. 34:29

Here YHWH acts because of His faithless leaders, but in Ezek. 36:27-36 He acts because
of His people's inability to be faithful and obedient to His Mosaic covenant. This default on the part of
His people precipitates a new covenant based on God's actions and faithfulness (cf. Jer. 31:31-34)!
Jesus is the Good Shepherd (cf. John 10; Heb. 13:20; 1 Pet. 2:25).

verses.zh: 牧人在羊群四散的日子怎样寻找他的羊，我必照样寻找我的羊。这些羊在密云黑暗的日子散到各处，我必从那里救回它们来。
verses.en: As a shepherd seeks out his flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will seek out my flock. I will rescue them from all the places where they have been scattered on a cloudy, dark day.[NOTE:1]
notes: The imagery may reflect the overthrow of the Israelites by the Babylonians in 587/6 b.c.
verses.commentary:
34:12 "when he is among the scattered sheep" As a shepherd was present with his flock, so YHWH will be
personally present (i.e. for blessing and protection) with His people.

▣ "on a cloudy and gloomy day" This is an idiom for judgment (cf. Ezek. 30:3; Ps. 97:2; Joel 2:2;
Jer. 13:16; Zeph. 1:15), in this case Israel's (by Assyria) and Judah's (by Neo-Babylon) exile.

verses.zh: 我必从万民中领出它们，从各国内聚集它们，引导它们归回故土，也必在以色列山上―一切溪水旁边、境内一切可居之处―牧养它们。
verses.en: I will bring them out from among the peoples and gather them from foreign countries; I will bring them to their own land. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the streams and all the inhabited places of the land.

verses.zh: 我必在美好的草场牧养它们。它们的圈必在以色列高处的山上，它们必在佳美之圈中躺卧，也在以色列山肥美的草场吃草。
verses.en: In a good pasture I will feed them; the mountain heights of Israel will be their pasture. There they will lie down in a lush[NOTE:1] pasture, and they will feed on rich grass on the mountains of Israel.

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：我必亲自作我羊的牧人，使它们得以躺卧。
verses.en: I myself will feed my sheep and I myself will make them lie down, declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 失丧的，我必寻找；被逐的，我必领回；受伤的，我必缠裹；有病的，我必医治；只是肥的壮的，我必除灭，也要秉公牧养它们。
verses.en: I will seek the lost and bring back the strays; I will bandage the injured and strengthen the sick, but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them—with judgment!
verses.commentary:
34:16

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, NAB
"but the fat and strong I will

destroy"

NJB
"I shall watch over the fat

and healthy"

LXX
"I will guard the strong"

Peshitta
"I will protect the fat and

strong"

The MT has "I will destroy," BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil IMPERFECT
FIRST PERSON SINGULAR (שׁמד), but the ancient versions (LXX, Peshitta,
and Vulgate) have "I will preserve" or "I will watch," BDB 1036, KB 1581
(שׁמר). The context supports both.

- "preserve" fits the immediate verses (vv. 11-16a)

- "destroy" fits

- Ezek. 34:16b-c

- the larger context (cf. vv. 17-22)

The UBS Text Project, p. 117, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

verses.zh: 「我的羊群哪，论到你们，主耶和华如此说：我必在羊与羊中间、公绵羊与公山羊中间施行判断。
verses.en: “‘As for you, my sheep, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look, I am about to judge between one sheep and another, between rams and goats.
verses.commentary:
34:17 "As for you, My flock" Ezekiel is making a comparison between the future condition of

- the current leadership

- the people

▣ "I will judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the male goats" This refers to a judgment between
the strong and the weak, between the greedy shepherds and the true shepherds (cf. Ezek. 34:22).

verses.zh: 你们这些肥壮的羊，在美好的草场吃草还以为小事吗？剩下的草，你们竟用蹄践踏了；你们喝清水，剩下的水，你们竟用蹄搅浑了。
verses.en: Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture that you must trample the rest of your pastures with your feet? When you drink clean water, must you muddy the rest of the water by trampling it with your feet?
verses.commentary:
34:18 "Is it too slight a thing for you" This is an idiom of inappropriate actions (cf. Ezek. 16:20; Num. 16:9,13; Josh. 22:17; 2 Sam. 7:19; Isa. 7:13).

▣ Sheep do not like to feed in trampled pastures nor drink from muddied waters (cf. Psalm 23). The wealthy not only exploited the
weak, poor, and socially ostracized, they made it such that they could not prosper and become free of their situation. This violates many passages in
Leviticus and Deuteronomy about how the covenant people should treat each other.

verses.zh: 至于我的羊，只得吃你们所践踏的，喝你们所搅浑的。
verses.en: As for my sheep, they must eat what you trampled with your feet and drink what you have muddied with your feet!

verses.zh: 「所以，主耶和华如此说：我必在肥羊和瘦羊中间施行判断。
verses.en: “‘Therefore, this is what the Sovereign Lord says to them: Look, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.

verses.zh: 因为你们用胁用肩拥挤一切瘦弱的，又用角抵触，以致使它们四散。
verses.en: Because you push with your side and your shoulder, and thrust your horns at all the weak sheep until you scatter them abroad,[NOTE:1]
verses.commentary: 34:21 The leaders are described as aggressive male rams and goats that push and shove the people away.

verses.zh: 所以，我必拯救我的群羊不再作掠物；我也必在羊和羊中间施行判断。
verses.en: I will save my sheep; they will no longer be prey. I will judge between one sheep and another.

verses.zh: 我必立一牧人照管他们，牧养他们，就是我的仆人大卫。他必牧养他们，作他们的牧人。
verses.en: “‘I will set one shepherd over them, and he will feed them—namely, my servant David.[NOTE:1] He will feed them and will be their shepherd.
notes: The messianic king is here called “David” (see Jer 30:9 and Hos 3:5, as well as Isa 11:1 and Mic 5:2) because he will fulfill the Davidic royal ideal depicted in the prophets and royal psalms (see Pss 2; 89).
verses.commentary:
34:23 "one shepherd" This probably refers to a united Israel (i.e. the children of Jacob, seed of Abraham).
There will no longer be a divided monarchy as occurred in 922 B.C. (i.e.
Israel and Judah).

The LXX has "another shepherd."

- one ‒ אחד

- another ‒ אחר

The UBS Text Project, p. 118, gives option #2 a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

▣ "My servant" This is an honorific title used first of the Patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, cf. Deut. 9:27). It is used of Moses in Num. 12:7;
Deut. 34:5; and Josh. 1:1,2,13,15; 8:31,33; 11:12,15; 12:6; 13:8; 14:7; 18:7; 22:2,4,5. It is also used of Joshua after his death (i.e. Josh. 24:29).

In Isaiah it becomes a way of referring to Israel collectively, but also to the special coming son of David (cf. Isaiah 40-56). You can clearly
see this interplay between the corporate and individual in Isaiah 42. Note that Isa. 42:1 is quoted in the NT as referring to the Messiah (cf. Matt. 12:18-21), but
Ezek. 34:19 obviously refers to the people of God (cf. Ezek. 41:8-10; 44:21). This interplay (i.e. collective or individual) occurs in several of the "Servant Songs"
(cf. Ezek. 42:1-9; 49:1-7; 50:4-11; 52:13-53:12), which are unique to Isaiah.

Special Topic: My Servant

▣ "David" David became the ideal king (cf. Ezek. 34:24; 37:24; 2 Samuel 7; Ps. 18:50; 89; Isa. 9:6-7; 11:1-5; 16:5; 55:3-5; Jer. 23:5-6;
30:9; 33:15,17; Hosea 3:5; Micah 5:2-5). David was sinful (like all humans), but he had a heart for YHWH. He became a way of referring to the special coming king
of righteousness (see E. W. Hengstenber, Christology of the Old Testament, pp. 687-690).

Special Topic: OT Titles for the Special Coming One

verses.zh: 我―耶和华必作他们的　神，我的仆人大卫必在他们中间作王。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: I, the Lord, will be their God, and my servant David will be prince[NOTE:1] among them; I, the Lord, have spoken!
notes: The messianic king (“David”) is called both “king” and “prince” in 37:24-25. The use of the term “prince” for this king facilitates the contrast between this ideal ruler and the Davidic “princes” denounced in earlier prophecies (see 7:27; 12:10, 12; 19:1; 21:25; 22:6, 25).
verses.commentary:
34:24 "I, the Lord, will be their God, and My servant David will be a prince among them" These verses are
(i.e. Ezek. 34:23-24) parallels of Ezek. 37:24-25. It is obviously Messianic. Note the typical covenant language! This is reunification of the covenant
people under a Davidic monarch, as well as the fulfillment of YHWH's covenant blessings (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-28. Also note the
concluding phrase, which assures the fulfillment of this divine promise (cf. Amos 9:11-15).

Special Topic: Messiah

Special Topic: Messianic Era

Special Topic: Covenant

The questions related to these verses are

- when does it occur?

- who does it refer to?

Some try to relate this to the return under Zerubbabel (a prince of Judah, cf. Ezra 1:8; the exact relationship between Sheshbazzar
and Zerubbabel is disputed). Others note the continuing problems of the post-exilic period (see Haggai and Malachi) and assert that these ideal
conditions must refer to the future.

It seems best to me to see it as an eschatological setting because of

- the nature of prophecy (see D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks)

- the expansion of the NT into a universal gospel (i.e. Eph. 2:11-3:13)

- the symbolic nature of Ezek. 34-39, 40-41, which relates this to God's plans for a restored Israel in the Persian period. All prophecy is
conditional, even this one. God wanted to restore Israel and would have if only Israel wanted to and would have been obedient.

Does the "everlasting covenant" of Ezek. 16:60 and 37:26 (cf. Isa. 55:3; 61:8) refer to a realized OT community or the NT
human family? My presuppositional theology pushes me to option #2. For me as a historical-grammatical interpreter, the OT must stand on its
own as the word of God. I must interpret it in light of the original inspired author's intent. However, progressive revelation (i.e. Jesus' life, actions,
and teaching, plus NT authors) refocuses the message from a Jewish setting in Palestine to a universal gospel for all peoples (cf. Acts), thus
fulfilling the concept of monotheism and the universal promise of Gen. 3:15. These prophecies must be analyzed through two lenses (i.e. the OT and
the NT). Christianity is only true if the NT is the fulfillment of the OT and Jesus is the promised Messiah. The hope is wider than Israel. Genesis 3:15
is a promise to all the sons and daughters of Adam, not just Jews. There were no Jews in Genesis 3.

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

Special Topic: Why Do OT Covenant Promises Seem So Different from NT Covenant Promises?

Special Topic: The Gospel

▣ "I will be their God" The king of Israel was to be YHWH's representative (cf. 1 Samuel 8). This represents the ideal picture of a
society where God is the true King and the righteous leader is His visible representative!

verses.zh: 「我必与他们立平安的约，使恶兽从境内断绝，他们就必安居在旷野，躺卧在林中。
verses.en: “‘I will make a covenant of peace with them and will rid the land of wild beasts, so that they can live securely[NOTE:1] in the wilderness and even sleep in the woods.[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrase “live securely” occurs in Ezek 28:26; 38:8, 11, 14; 39:26 as an expression of freedom from fear. It is a promised blessing resulting from obedience (see Lev 26:5-6).
The woods were typically considered to be places of danger (Ps 104:20-21; Jer 5:6).
verses.commentary:
34:25 "I will make a covenant of peace" This term "peace" is the Hebrew Shalom (BDB 1022, cf. Ezek. 37:24-28; 39:25-29; Lev. 26:6.
It must be remembered that all covenants have obligations. Free creatures have options!

Is this "covenant of peace" the same as "the new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34? Ezekiel 36:22-36 (like these texts) describes a new
way that YHWH will relate to His covenant people, a way characterized by (1) a new heart and a new mind and (2) YHWH's personal action on their behalf.
A new covenant initially focuses on God's graciousness in redemption, but still desires a righteous people to draw "the nations" to Himself!

Special Topic: Peace (OT)

Special Topic: Covenant

▣ "eliminate harmful beasts from the land" As is so often the case, Ezekiel is influenced by
Leviticus 26 (i.e. Ezek. 34:22) and Deuteronomy 28 (i.e. 32:24). The curses of disobedience are reversed into
the blessing of covenant fidelity. The blessing was always YHWH's intent. He wanted to attract the nations
to Himself by blessing Israel.

The prophecy of the new age is Isa. 11:6-9; 65:25, which includes animals and shows the
original intent of Eden (i.e. a place of fellowship between God and humanity, and humanity and the animal
kingdom). The Bible starts with an Edenic setting and also ends the same way (cf. Revelation 21-22). Heaven
is depicted as a recreated Garden of Eden. Animals are part of this depiction!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan)

▣ "so that they may live securely" This was part of the promises of Deuteronomy, which Ezekiel
restates (cf. Ezek. 28:26; 34:27,28; 38:8,11,14; 39:26; Jer. 33:16). Their security is because of the
presence of God!

verses.zh: 我必使他们与我山的四围成为福源，我也必叫时雨落下，必有福如甘霖而降。
verses.en: I will turn them and the regions around my hill into a blessing. I will make showers come down in their season; they will be showers that bring blessing.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “showers of blessing.” Abundant rain, which in turn produces fruit and crops (v. 27), is a covenantal blessing for obedience (Lev 26:4).
verses.commentary:
34:26 "My hill" This is a reference to Jerusalem and specifically the temple mount (cf. Ezek. 20:40-49). YHWH's hill is a contrast to the
worship of the fertility gods of Canaan on both natural and manmade hills.

The prophecy, which is typical of the prophets, refers to a restored Jerusalem. Must this be taken literally? This is a central
issue in dispensational theology. I have come to a different conclusion. For a good critique of dispensationalism see Steve Gregg's YouTube video,
Deconstructing Dispensationalism

▣ "I will cause showers" Moisture at the appropriate time and in expected amounts was part of the
covenant blessings of Lev. 26:4 and Deut. 28:12. These were agricultural people living in an arid climate.
Society was based on the regular and expected cycles of the seasons! YHWH controls the cycle and the seasons
(i.e. Lev. 25:21).

The phrase "showers of blessings" reflects the agricultural nature of God's promised blessings to obedient
descendants of the Patriarchs (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28).

Special Topic: Waters

verses.zh: 田野的树必结果，地也必有出产；他们必在故土安然居住。我折断他们所负的轭，救他们脱离那以他们为奴之人的手；那时，他们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: The trees of the field will yield their fruit and the earth will yield its crops. They will live securely on their land; they will know that I am the Lord, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
verses.commentary:
34:27 "a tree of the field will yield its fruit" This refers to the covenant abundance (cf. Deuteronomy 27;
Hosea 2:22; Joel 3:18; Amos 9:13, 14; Zech. 8:12).

▣ "I have broken the bars of their yoke" This is an idiom of oppression first used in Lev. 26:13. So
much of Ezekiel's vocabulary and theology comes from Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29.

▣ "hand" See Special Topic: Hand

verses.zh: 他们必不再作外邦人的掠物，地上的野兽也不再吞吃他们；却要安然居住，无人惊吓。
verses.en: They will no longer be prey for the nations, and the wild beasts will not devour them. They will live securely, and no one will make them afraid.
verses.commentary:
34:28-29 The nations will no longer dominate YHWH's people. This is the result of the original covenant
coming into reality!

Special Topic: Covenant Promises to the Patriarchs

verses.zh: 我必给他们兴起有名的植物；他们在境内不再为饥荒所灭，也不再受外邦人的羞辱，
verses.en: I will prepare for them a healthy[NOTE:1] planting. They will no longer be victims[NOTE:2] of famine in the land and will no longer bear the insults of the nations.
notes: The MT reads לְשֵׁם (leshem, “for a name”), meaning perhaps a renowned planting (place). The translation takes this to be a metathesis of שָׁלֹם (shalom), as was read by the LXX.
verses.commentary:
34:29

NASB
"a renowned planting"

NKJV
"a garden of renown"

NRSV, NJB
"a splendid vegetation"

TEV
"fertile fields"

JPSOA
"a planting of renown"

NIV
"a land of renown"

REB
"their crops renowned"

Peshitta
"a plantation of peace"

LXX
"a plant of peace"

The word "planting" (מטע, BDB 642) can mean the plant itself or where it is planted. So the text is referring to

- God's people's crops and herds being very productive (i.e. evidence covenant restored, which is the fruitfulness and safety described in Ezek. 34:25-27)

- God's people going back to Palestine (evidence covenant restored).

The LXX and Peshitta reverse two consonants in the PREPOSITION plus the NOUN
"renown/name" (לשׁם, BDB 1027) and change it to "peace" (שׁלם, BDB 1023) to link up with
Ezek. 34:25 (i.e. "I will make a covenant of peace").

This imagery goes back to Ezek. 17:22-24 and the opposite of Ezek. 19:10-14 (cf. Isa. 60:21; 61:3).
One of the titles for the Messiah is "Branch" (cf. Isa. 4:2). There is a mixing of images here.

- the cosmic tree (i.e. Ezekiel 31)

- Israel as a plant (or planting place, which is parallel to Ezek. 34:26a)

- the Messiah as a shoot or branch from a stump (cf. Isa. 11:2,10; 53:2; Rom. 15:12)

Special Topic: Peace (shalom)

Special Topic: The Branch of the Lord

verses.zh: 必知道我、耶和华―他们的　神是与他们同在的，并知道他们―以色列家是我的民。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Then they will know that I, the Lord their God, am with them[NOTE:1] and that they are my people, the house of Israel, declares the Sovereign Lord.[NOTE:2]
notes: A promise given to Abraham (Gen 15:7) and his descendants (Gen 15:8; Exod 6:7).
The blessings described in vv. 25-30 are those promised for obedience in Lev 26:4-13.
verses.commentary:
34:30 "I the Lord their God am with them" These are Covenant terms which show
that the Covenant has been restored in the midst of the destruction of the temple! There is no more significant
statement than "I am with them" (i.e. Emmanuel, i.e. Isa. 7:14).

verses.zh: 你们作我的羊，我草场上的羊，乃是以色列人，我也是你们的　神。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: And you, my sheep, the sheep of my pasture, are my people,[NOTE:1] and I am your God, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”
notes: Heb, “the sheep of my pasture, you are human.” See 36:37-38 for a similar expression. The possessive pronoun “my” is supplied in the translation to balance “I am your God” in the next clause.
verses.commentary:
34:31 This covenant language about God as Shepherd (cf. John 10) and His people as sheep is also found in
Psalm 23; 78:52; 80:1; Isa. 40:11; Jer. 31:10). This is such a wonderful metaphor of personal presence, care,
protection, and provision!

▣ "you are men, and I am your God" This is not meant to be an emphasis on transcendence, but on the
special creation of humanity (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 2:7-8). The LXX omits "you are men" and it is followed by RSV,
REB, NAB. Because "men" are mentioned in parallel texts in this literary unit of Ezekiel (i.e. Ezek. 36:37,38),
it seems best to stay with the MT.
